The answer is D - the foramen ovale. This is the structure that is supposed to close to prevent a left-to-right shunt. The right atria will have a higher pressure than the left atria in the neonate due to the fact that the lungs are collapsed and not inflating. This will mean that blood will go from the right side to the left side through the foramen ovale. Once the lungs are inflated, then oxygenated blood will be in the left atria and deoxygenated blood in the right atria. This will mean that the left side will be under higher pressure and blood will go from the left atria to the right atria. This will cause the septum to close. The foramen ovale will usually be completely closed after 1 month.
